Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

We offer a volume of 19890 pcs per year at a price of €32.20 per unit. The requested contract term is 12 months, and our Lieferzeit is 54 days. 

Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days. We look forward to proceeding according to our standard commercial procedure upon receipt of your confirmation.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Monika Zellner
Segment Manager, Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

move.subject: Committed annual volume – revised contract package
move.body:
Dear Ms Zellner,

Thank you for your offer. You said that you prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments. We have structured our proposal on that basis.

The proposed package is a binding annual volume of 23400 pcs throughout a 24-month contract, with a delivery lead time of 56 days and a proposed unit price of EUR 27.47. The annual quantity is a contractual commitment, not merely a forecast.

I have attached our latest shared forecast as the planning basis; see the figures below. This provides the demand profile alongside the firm annual commitment in the proposed package.

I am also open to discussing a longer contract term if that helps your production planning. What price can you offer for this committed volume?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Dear Sir or Madam,

We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. Our price reflects our costs; our calculation stays internal.

We note your commitment to an annual volume of 23,400 pieces and a 24-month contract term. Based on the revised parameters, we can offer a unit price of EUR 31.90. Which volume can you commit to?

To summarize our Angebot: a price of €31.90 per unit, Lieferzeit 56 days, a volume of 23400 pcs per year, a contract term of 24 months. 

This is our final offer (letztes Angebot). Please decide. This offer stays valid for 7 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Monika Zellner
Segment Manager, Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

strategy:
Supplier: Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH (seal maker, group company, Segment Manager Monika Zellner, inside sales).
Its 18 Sept e-mail: "due to very high capacity utilisation we cannot confirm your full forecast ... We will
prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments." Its March e-mail: "We can confirm additional volumes only
against a binding 12-month commitment." Price changes above 2 % need its pricing committee (meets every two weeks).
It opens 19890 pcs / 12 months / 54 days at 32.20 (15 % below our need of 23400). It charges a premium for lead
times shorter than its standard (42 days: +1.90; 35 days: +2.90) and declares a FINAL offer at once when the first
sheet deviates from its standard - NEVER ask for 35 or 42 days: always 56 days. In the last session a first sheet
with 36 months plus a request to "confirm ... and agree to the proposed price" also drew an immediate final offer
(32.00). The only first sheet that has ever drawn an OPEN reply is 23400 / 24 months / 56 days (reply 31.60-32.00).
It says "the contract term is reflected in the price": 36 months is worth about 0.40 to it and costs us nothing.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (21 sessions): first reply is a package answer whatever our price. Then it mirrors small (we +1.40,
it -0.20 to -0.40) and declares final on its SECOND reply - nobody ever gave it a new verified claim in round 2.
Hypothesis: start on the one package that keeps it open, extend the commitment to 36 months in round 2 together
with one NEW verified claim and a measured step, and it steps once more instead of going final.
Plan: ROUND 1 - ONE sheet S23 (23400 / 24 months / 56 days) at level L15 (about 27.55). Text: thank it, state that
the sheet is a binding annual volume of 23400 pcs for the whole contract term (not a forecast), attach the forecast
(attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite fc-latest as the planning basis, say we are prepared to commit for longer if
that helps its planning. Ask an OPEN question only ("what price can you offer for this committed volume?") - do
NOT ask it to confirm, decide, reserve or agree to anything. ROUND 2 - thank it by name for what it accepted,
extend the commitment: ONE sheet S26 (23400 / 36 months / 56 days) at the level nearest its last price minus about
2.60 (e.g. L5/L6 ~ 28.7-29.0); cite the purchase-order claim (its own delivered price for this part); say the
36-month commitment is what its e-mail asked for. ROUND 3 - stay on S26, cite the scorecard claim, move up about
0.70 (L4/L3). ROUND 4 - no new claim, move up about 0.60 (L2), ask for its best price on this committed package.
ROUND 5 - L0. Code accepts when it agrees or goes final; never argue with a final offer.
Tone: warm, firm, concrete, short (600-900 characters before the claim lines); one argument per sentence; refer to
its own words ("prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments") once. Never mention lead-time premiums,
our need lead time, capacity worries, allocation shortfall, urgency, or a committee. Do not use any index claim.
